detail: Supersedes the 'unresolved, two parallel environments' entry earlier tonight. Nash confirmed miniforge3 base is canonical: has sklearn/pandas/torch/transformers/sentence-transformers/everything, full path /Users/nash/miniforge3/bin/python3. Do NOT use /Users/nash/Projects/ConspiracyComments/.venv (Python 3.9.6, legacy) for anything new. ALSO FOUND WORSE, same night: a session (this one) accidentally used a THIRD, completely undocumented environment -- /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 (system Homebrew Python 3.14.6, almost nothing installed, not sklearn/pandas/torch/anything) -- because bare `python3` on PATH resolves there, not to miniforge3, despite conda auto_activate_base=True actually being set correctly. ROOT CAUSE, confirmed by reading ~/.zshrc directly: line 50 does `export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"` AFTER the conda-init block (lines 5-18) that prepends miniforge3/bin -- so homebrew's python3 always shadows miniforge3's on every new shell, a one-line PATH-ordering bug in the dotfile, not a conda misconfiguration. NOT fixed at the dotfile level this session (Nash's call whether to reorder those two blocks in ~/.zshrc, flagged rather than edited unasked). Fixed at the project-script level instead: any script needing real packages should never rely on bare `python3` -- either invoke /Users/nash/miniforge3/bin/python3 explicitly, or the script's own header should assert its interpreter has the expected packages and fail loudly if not, rather than silently running in whatever `python3` happened to resolve to.

name: checkpoint portability confirmed -- no migration needed to consolidate onto miniforge3
detail: Directly tested (not assumed): outputs/checkpoints/binconf_other015_binary_confidence/model_state.pt (a real project checkpoint, produced under .venv's Python 3.9.6) loads cleanly under ~/miniforge3's Python 3.12.12 + torch 2.8.0 -- torch.load succeeded, all 174 state_dict keys present and correctly named. This is expected and general: PyTorch checkpoints (state_dict .pt files, safetensors, sklearn .joblib) are serialized tensor/parameter DATA, not Python bytecode -- they aren't tied to the Python version that produced them, only to the tensor/array library's ability to deserialize the storage FORMAT, which is stable across minor torch/Python versions for standard state_dict structures (the only real risk case is a checkpoint that pickled a custom Python class definition alongside the tensors, which this project's checkpoints don't appear to do). CONCLUSION: there is no 'environment merge' problem to solve and no checkpoint migration cost -- consolidating onto miniforge3 (already decided canonical, see the entry above) as the one Python used for all new local work does not require re-training, re-exporting, or touching any existing checkpoint. The .venv (Python 3.9.6) can simply stop being used going forward; nothing needs to be actively migrated OUT of it.

name: real risk found: sklearn .joblib checkpoints throw InconsistentVersionWarning under miniforge3, unlike torch checkpoints which load clean
detail: Direct test, not assumed: data/processed/stance_classifier_2stage_pooled.joblib and staged_pipeline_models.joblib (both pickled under sklearn 1.7.2, per the warning text) load WITHOUT crashing under miniforge3's sklearn 1.9.0 -- but sklearn itself raises InconsistentVersionWarning for TfidfTransformer/TfidfVectorizer/LogisticRegression on every load, explicitly stating 'This might lead to breaking code or invalid results. Use at your own risk.' This is a DIFFERENT and more serious risk class than the torch checkpoint portability already confirmed fine (see the checkpoint_portability_confirmed entry) -- sklearn pickles serialize actual Python object internals (estimator implementation details), which CAN silently change behavior across minor versions, unlike torch state_dicts which are just tensor blobs. NOT YET VERIFIED whether this actually changes any real output (e.g. whether stance_classifier_2stage_pooled.joblib's predictions on a known val set still match previously-recorded numbers under sklearn 1.9.0 vs whatever produced the 1.7.2 pickle) -- that spot-check is the concrete next step before trusting any sklearn-joblib-based script's output post-env-consolidation. Also unrelated to and should not be confused with the separate PyABSA 'external compatibility rot' issue (transformers API change breaking an old third-party pretrained checkpoint, see task_2026-08-20_session_handoff_paraphrase_stability doc) -- that's a different library, different failure mode (hard crash, not a silent-drift warning), and was already known/logged before tonight.
status: unverified -- loads without crashing but sklearn's own warning flags real risk of silent behavior change; needs a known-output spot-check before treating sklearn-joblib-based scripts as safe under the new consolidated env
